methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series D → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.5x) to $2.0B last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.0B - $2.3B.

data.narrative:
Exotec, a Series D robotics and manufacturing automation company, has raised over $335M and carries a post-money valuation of $2.0B. The valuation framework relies on a peer universe of nine comparable companies: one public (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private-stage peers including Divergent, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity. The immediate peer set for triangulation comprises four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies ranging from Series C to Series E.

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression approach, anchored to the $2.0B last post-money and applying a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical for Series D advancement, implies a valuation of $3.0B. Peer-median analysis across four robotics comparables (Divergent at $2.3B, Hadrian at $1.6B, Agile Robots at $1.0B, and Nimble Robotics at $1.0B) yields a median valuation of $1.3B, with a range of $1.0B to $2.3B. The disparity between methods reflects heterogeneity in peer stage composition and capital efficiency.

Triangulation across both methods yields a range of $1.1B (low) to $3.4B (high), with a median of $2.1B. The current $2.0B valuation sits near the midpoint and aligns with stage-progression logic but sits above peer-median estimates. Key uncertainties include capital intensity and path to next-stage funding, as well as divergence in peer monetization timelines within the fragmented robotics sector.
